question: With the historical route estimator held fixed, does replacing each coarse live-query update by direct depth PnP on every causal RGB transition remove the observed turn-heavy live-motion chain breaks?
claim_scope: result-dependent consumed live-motion mechanism gate only; no navigation or generalization claim
selection_rule: first three formal route-tangent geometry failures whose historical route initialized and whose typed failure edge was a live_query_adjacent_sample, in benchmark-manifest order

excluded_initialization_failure.reason: its failure occurred while constructing the historical route, so it cannot test a live-query-only intervention

observed_parent_failures.history_0: coarse live interval 8 frames, 33.64 deg yaw, direct PnP had 7 matches
observed_parent_failures.history_1: coarse live interval 6 frames, 26.31 deg yaw, direct PnP had 13 matches
observed_parent_failures.history_6: coarse live interval 8 frames, 30.32 deg yaw, direct PnP had 1 match

candidate.historical_route_motion: unchanged Fundamental-MAGSAC followed by depth PnP
candidate.live_query_motion: direct depth PnP on every causal RGB transition within each controller interval
candidate.depth: same frozen LingBot relative-depth head and first-40 camera-height scale receipt
candidate.controller_payload: unchanged canonical unit bearing at fixed 2.5 m radius

pass_rule.query_sampling: every available frame transition after route initialization

decision.pass: authorize a consumed full-population dense-live-query plus frozen support-projection attribution; any navigation claim still requires a newly frozen fresh population
decision.fail: do not relax PnP thresholds or add a controller fallback; inspect the first failed atomic RGB transition and test a continuous prediction-plus-evidence route-state estimator
